prompts.text: Who in your circle always turns a casual introduction into a memorable story?
Tell me about somebody you met through an awkward first conversation that eventually became funny.
Two friends independently offer to introduce you to the same person. How do you handle the coincidence?
Meet someone over a playful group quiz or during an unplanned conversation at a café?
A slightly embarrassing first impression sometimes makes a better friendship story.
People often reveal their sense of humour in the way they introduce their friends.
What's the most unexpected thing you've had in common with a new acquaintance?
Recall the first time someone remembered an oddly specific detail about you.
Your friends must describe you to a newcomer using only three harmless clues. What would they choose?
Let a friend write your introduction or introduce yourself with one surprising fact?
Which friend gives compliments that sound like an award acceptance speech?
Describe a time an unexpected compliment made everybody around you laugh.
A friend invents a yearly award for the most thoughtful person in your group. Who would you nominate and why?
Receive a funny handmade certificate or a sincere voice note from your friends?
The most convincing compliments are often about habits nobody notices publicly.
Different people feel appreciated through attention, useful favours or specific words.
What's a compliment you've wanted to give someone but struggled to phrase?
Tell me about somebody thanking you for a small gesture you'd forgotten.
You must write a cheerful introduction for a friend receiving an imaginary award. What's your opening line?
Celebrate a friend's success with a quiet meal or a surprise group cheer?
Which friendship habit would make a hilariously bad official rule?
Recall a time a friendly argument over a tiny detail lasted longer than the original event.
Your group elects a referee for disagreements about where to eat. Who gets the whistle?
Vote on the next hangout or let the person who arrived earliest choose?
Some of the funniest group traditions begin as compromises nobody intended to repeat.
Every friendship group seems to have somebody who remembers the exact wording of old jokes.
What's a silly disagreement you and a friend still laugh about?
Tell me about changing your opinion simply because a friend's explanation was entertaining.
Two friends insist they invented the same catchphrase. How would you settle the dispute?
Keep score in harmless debates or agree that nobody ever wins?
What harmless habit of yours would your family tease you about at a reunion?
Describe the day a relative caught you pretending you knew how to do something.
Your family stages a talent show based on skills nobody normally celebrates. What would your entry be?
Let your siblings choose your karaoke song or let your cousins choose your dance style?
Family nicknames are funniest when everybody, including the person named, enjoys them.
Relatives sometimes remember childhood versions of us that feel like entirely different people.
Who in your family is best at turning a small mishap into an epic story?
Tell me about a funny family misunderstanding that was cleared up over dinner.
Your childhood self arrives at a family gathering today. Who would recognise you first?
Hear a parent's funniest school story or a grandparent's most mischievous childhood adventure?
What's a playful way someone has reminded you to keep in touch?
Recall a message from an old friend that instantly brought back your shared humour.
You and a friend must create a secret greeting for your next reunion. What does it involve?
Send a ridiculous postcard or leave a thoughtful voice message with a funny ending?
A long friendship is partly a collection of references nobody else fully understands.
Some friends recognise each other's moods from a single word in a message.
Which phrase from a friend would make you laugh even in the middle of a busy day?
Tell me about reconnecting with someone through a joke you both remembered.
A friend accidentally sends you a message meant for the group chat. What's a kind way to respond?
Recreate an old photo with friends or record a playful reunion interview?
Which person do you trust to plan a surprise that would suit your personality?
Tell me about a friend who noticed you needed company without making a fuss.
Your friends plan a surprise outing but deliberately leave one clue. What clue would you want?
A mystery destination chosen by a friend or a familiar favourite with a surprise guest?
The best surprises respect the recipient's preferences more than the organiser's ambitions.
A small shared ritual sometimes feels more personal than an expensive celebration.
What's the funniest harmless surprise somebody has arranged for you?
Describe a surprise you planned that required a lot more coordination than expected.
You have ten minutes to plan a cheerful welcome for a returning friend. What would you do?
Hide a thoughtful note in a friend's bag or send a perfectly timed celebratory message?
Which social situation makes you switch into your most awkward version of yourself?
Tell me about trying to impress somebody and accidentally making them laugh instead.
You forget the name of somebody who's greeted you warmly three times. How do you recover?
Accidentally wave at a stranger or laugh at a joke before hearing the ending?
Admitting a small social mistake usually makes it less embarrassing.
People often bond faster over a harmless shared blunder than a polished introduction.
What's the most creative way you've recovered from greeting the wrong person?
Recall a time someone helped you escape an awkward pause with an unexpected question.
A new friend mispronounces your name with great confidence. How do you correct them kindly?
Have a friend rescue you from small talk or take over and ask an unusual question?
Who in your friendship circle always has an unexpectedly good recommendation?
Tell me about accepting a friend's suggestion and finding a new favourite place.
A friend wants to introduce you to their hobby, but you know nothing about it. What's your first question?
Trade favourite songs with a friend or swap recommendations for underrated films?
Taking someone's recommendation seriously is one way to learn their tastes.
Friendships grow in surprising directions when people share interests they initially kept private.
What's an interest you picked up because somebody close to you cared about it?
Describe a time you introduced two friends who unexpectedly became inseparable.
Two people you like have opposite tastes in entertainment. What activity might help them bond?
Attend a friend's favourite concert or invite them to your favourite exhibition?
What playful challenge would reveal how well your friends know you?
Tell me about a time a friend guessed your preference with suspicious accuracy.
Your friends compete to choose your ideal weekend using only five questions. What would you ask them?
Guess each other's childhood hobbies or predict each other's travel preferences?
Knowing which tiny inconvenience annoys someone is an underrated sign of familiarity.
People who spend time together sometimes develop matching gestures without noticing.
Which mannerism have you accidentally picked up from someone close to you?
Recall a time you and a friend said the same unusual thing at once.
Someone asks your closest friend to order your usual meal. How accurately would they manage?
Compare your old answers to a friendship quiz or take a brand-new one together?
What's one harmless way you'd like your friends to be more spontaneous?
Describe a day when a quick invitation turned into a meaningful new connection.
Your group has two free hours and no budget for tickets. Who gets to suggest the plan?
Invite someone new to an established tradition or start a fresh activity with old friends?
Friendships stay interesting when people occasionally let each other choose the unfamiliar option.
The best group plans often leave room for people who prefer an early exit.
Who in your circle would enjoy an impromptu walk and an unhurried conversation?
Tell me about meeting a friend's friend and realising you'd crossed paths years earlier.
A friend proposes a reunion where everyone brings one unexpected guest. What ground rules would you suggest?
End an outing by planning the next date or leave everybody to suggest ideas later?
